Lagodekhi (Tsitelgori) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Tsitelgori, Georgia

Not demolished. This cemetery is tied to a unique episode of Soviet Jewish history: the Tsiteli Gora collective farm, established in 1928 near Lagodekhi as part of a Soviet-era push (led by the OZET land management society) to involve Georgian Jews in agriculture. Settlers received state subsidies to build homes; by 1929 the farm had 15 two-story dwellings housing 25 families, growing to 40 households by 1930 and 82 by 1940, complete with a school, kindergarten, and medical point. Tsiteli Gora was the only Jewish collective farm in Georgia to survive OZET's liquidation in the late 1930s, remaining active until the 1970s, when most of its Jewish residents emigrated to Israel and were replaced by Georgian newcomers. No synagogue was ever officially registered on site - residents reportedly traveled to Tbilisi for services. The cemetery was established alongside the collective farm; its earliest tombstone dates to 1935, and after a gap of roughly four decades following the 1970s emigration wave, a single burial occurred in 2014.
